topic: Can we achieve a situation where essentially every material can be recycled and reused?
research_question: For a defined material-product stream and required service, under what combinations of product design, information, collection, sorting, processing, market demand, and policy can a high fraction of material deliver repeated future service without increasing life-cycle environmental burdens, toxicity, or social cost?

candidate_routes.name: design_for_recovery_grammar
candidate_routes.reason: constrains material families, joins, labels, and additives to improve separation and quality

candidate_routes.name: quality_aware_dynamic_routing
candidate_routes.reason: routes objects by measured state to reuse, refurbishment, mechanical recovery, chemical recovery, or controlled treatment

candidate_routes.name: regional_circularity_contracts
candidate_routes.reason: links accepted design grades to stable buyers, producer responsibility, and residue ownership

candidate_routes.name: circularity_portfolio_optimizer
candidate_routes.reason: compares reduction, reuse, repair, recycling, chemical recovery, treatment, and substitution across product and region scenarios

candidate_routes.name: controlled_exclusion_and_safe_sink
candidate_routes.reason: prevents unsafe recycling claims for hazardous, contaminated, mixed, or dissipative streams

required_boundaries: reduction and reuse compete with recycling
downcycling is reported as changed service rather than closed-loop equivalence
hazardous and dissipative streams can require controlled treatment or substitution
private profitability is separated from social value
